clinician.trajectory_summary: A 49-year-old woman presented on October 4, 2022, with 20 days of cognitive symptoms including difficulty finding words, unresponsiveness, decreased memory and orientation (MMSE 23), and apathetic expression. Neurological examination revealed no limb weakness or facial asymmetry. MRI showed a chronic cortical infarct in the left frontal lobe. Vascular imaging (MRA and carotid ultrasound) demonstrated no stenosis or occlusion. The patient had no classical cerebrovascular risk factors (hypertension, dyslipidemia, diabetes, smoking) and no prior history of thrombosis or recurrent pregnancy loss. Immunological examination revealed positive antibodies to vimentin/cardiolipin complex and anti-annexin A5 antibody, establishing the diagnosis of seronegative antiphospholipid syndrome (SN-APS). The diagnosis was confirmed by the subsequent recurrent thrombotic event: on July 21, 2023, the patient presented with acute right limb weakness, dysarthria, global aphasia, right facial palsy, and right hemiparesis (MRC 3/5) with NIHSS score of 11. Post-thrombolysis imaging (alteplase 50 mg) revealed left temporal insular lobe infarcts with small hemorrhagic transformation of the basal ganglia (~2ml), with no venous thrombosis or arteriovenous malformations on MRV. Cardiac evaluation identified a patent foramen ovale (PFO, approximately 3 mm) on transesophageal echocardiogram. The patient underwent transcatheter PFO closure after hemorrhage absorption and achieved good functional outcomes at discharge (mRS 1) on dual antiplatelet therapy and atorvastatin.
